modules.title: Replication and High Availability
modules.goal: Keep a second copy ready and understand lag, failover and split-brain risks.

topics.title: Replication Basics
topics.simple: Replication data ko doosre node par copy karta hai.
topics.pro: Replication streams changes from a primary to one or more replicas for availability and read scaling.

topics.title: Streaming Replication
topics.simple: Streaming replication WAL continuously bhejta hai.
topics.pro: Physical streaming replication ships WAL records to a standby that applies them continuously.
points: Lag is measured in WAL bytes or time.

example.sql: SELECT application_name, state, sync_state FROM pg_stat_replication;

topics.title: Logical Replication
topics.simple: Logical replication selected changes publish karta hai.
topics.pro: Logical replication decodes WAL into row changes and applies them through publications and subscriptions.
points: It does not copy the whole cluster.

example.sql: CREATE PUBLICATION app_pub FOR TABLE students, courses;

topics.title: Primary and Replica
topics.simple: Primary writes leta hai; replica read-only hota hai.
topics.pro: A hot standby accepts read-only queries while applying WAL, so reporting can be isolated from write load.

topics.title: Synchronous vs Asynchronous
topics.simple: Sync replication commit wait karta hai; async nahi.
topics.pro: Synchronous replication waits for a standby acknowledgement before commit, trading latency for lower data loss.
points: Sync can block writes if the standby is slow.

topics.title: Failover
topics.simple: Failover replica ko primary banata hai.
topics.pro: Failover promotes a standby when the primary fails, ideally through an orchestrator that fences the old primary.

topics.title: Replication Lag
topics.simple: Lag replica ki primary se doori batata hai.
topics.pro: Lag is the delay between a primary commit and its visibility on a replica, measured in time or LSN.

topics.title: Read Scaling
topics.simple: Replicas read traffic distribute karte hain.
topics.pro: Read replicas offload reporting and read-heavy endpoints, but applications must tolerate stale reads.
points: Do not send writes to replicas.
Handle lag-sensitive reads on the primary.

example.output: A read that can run on a replica.

topics.title: Promotion
topics.simple: Promotion replica ko writable banata hai.
topics.pro: Promotion ends recovery and makes the standby a primary; it must be coordinated with client routing and fencing.

topics.title: Split Brain
topics.simple: Split brain do primaries ko accept karne ki state hai.
topics.pro: Split brain happens when the old primary and the promoted standby both accept writes, causing divergent data.

example.sql: -- Fence the old primary before promotion

topics.title: Conflict Handling
topics.simple: Logical replication conflicts resolve karne padte hain.
topics.pro: Logical replication can conflict on primary keys or constraints; the subscription can stop or skip depending on configuration.

topics.title: Replication Slots
topics.simple: Slot WAL retention ko control karta hai.
topics.pro: A replication slot prevents WAL removal until the consumer catches up, which protects replicas but can fill disk.

example.sql: SELECT slot_name, active, restart_lsn FROM pg_replication_slots;

topics.title: Monitoring Replication
topics.simple: Lag, state aur slots monitor karo.
topics.pro: Monitoring tracks replication state, lag, slot retention and failover readiness.

topics.title: Failover Testing
topics.simple: Failover ko regularly test karo.
topics.pro: A failover drill measures promotion time, application reconnection and data loss against RTO and RPO.

topics.title: Read-Your-Writes
topics.simple: Lag-sensitive reads primary se karo.
topics.pro: After a write, a replica may not yet show it; route that user’s next read to the primary or wait for the LSN.

topics.title: Connection Routing
topics.simple: Clients ko primary aur replicas ke behes route karo.
topics.pro: A router or load balancer sends writes to the primary and reads to replicas, with health checks and failover awareness.

topics.title: Common Replication Errors
topics.simple: Lag, full disk aur split brain common failures hain.
topics.pro: Common failures are an inactive slot filling disk, a replica promoted while the old primary still writes, and reads routed to a lagging replica.

example.sql: SELECT slot_name, pg_size_pretty(pg_wal_lsn_diff(pg_current_wal_lsn(), restart_lsn)) AS retained FROM pg_replication_slots;

topics.title: High Availability Design
topics.simple: HA ke liye redundancy, health checks aur failover chahiye.
topics.pro: High availability combines replicas, automated health checks, quorum and tested failover, not just a standby.

example.sql: -- primary plus synchronous standby plus witness

topics.title: Backup vs Replica
topics.simple: Replica backup nahi hai.
topics.pro: A replica protects availability but does not protect against accidental deletes, corruption or ransomware without separate backups.

example.sql: -- Keep a separate encrypted backup even with replicas

topics.title: Practical HA Runbook
topics.simple: Detect, fence, promote, redirect, verify.
topics.pro: A runbook makes failover deterministic: detect the failure, fence the old primary, promote the standby, redirect clients and verify writes.

interview.q: Module 33 · Explain Replication Basics in a production query.
interview.answer: Replication streams changes from a primary to one or more replicas for availability and read scaling. Key rules: Primary accepts writes. Replicas receive changes. Replication is not backup.

interview.q: Module 33 · Explain Streaming Replication in a production query.
interview.answer: Physical streaming replication ships WAL records to a standby that applies them continuously. Key rules: It copies the cluster. It supports hot standby reads. Lag is measured in WAL bytes or time.

interview.q: Module 33 · Explain Logical Replication in a production query.
interview.answer: Logical replication decodes WAL into row changes and applies them through publications and subscriptions. Key rules: It is table-level. It can cross versions. It does not copy the whole cluster.

interview.q: Module 33 · Explain Primary and Replica in a production query.
interview.answer: A hot standby accepts read-only queries while applying WAL, so reporting can be isolated from write load. Key rules: Writes go to the primary. Replicas can serve reads. Replica reads can be stale.

interview.q: Module 33 · Explain Synchronous vs Asynchronous in a production query.
interview.answer: Synchronous replication waits for a standby acknowledgement before commit, trading latency for lower data loss. Key rules: Sync reduces RPO. Async is faster. Sync can block writes if the standby is slow.

interview.q: Module 33 · Explain Failover in a production query.
interview.answer: Failover promotes a standby when the primary fails, ideally through an orchestrator that fences the old primary. Key rules: Promote the standby. Redirect clients. Prevent split brain.

interview.q: Module 33 · Explain Replication Lag in a production query.
interview.answer: Lag is the delay between a primary commit and its visibility on a replica, measured in time or LSN. Key rules: Lag grows under load. Read-your-writes can fail. Monitor continuously.

interview.q: Module 33 · Explain Read Scaling in a production query.
interview.answer: Read replicas offload reporting and read-heavy endpoints, but applications must tolerate stale reads. Key rules: Route reads deliberately. Do not send writes to replicas. Handle lag-sensitive reads on the primary.

interview.q: Module 33 · Explain Promotion in a production query.
interview.answer: Promotion ends recovery and makes the standby a primary; it must be coordinated with client routing and fencing. Key rules: Promote once. Fence the old primary. Update connection strings.

interview.q: Module 33 · Explain Split Brain in a production query.
interview.answer: Split brain happens when the old primary and the promoted standby both accept writes, causing divergent data. Key rules: Use fencing. Use a quorum. Reconcile carefully.

interview.q: Module 33 · Explain Conflict Handling in a production query.
interview.answer: Logical replication can conflict on primary keys or constraints; the subscription can stop or skip depending on configuration. Key rules: Monitor conflicts. Design keys carefully. Decide skip versus stop.

interview.q: Module 33 · Explain Replication Slots in a production query.
interview.answer: A replication slot prevents WAL removal until the consumer catches up, which protects replicas but can fill disk. Key rules: Monitor slot lag. Drop unused slots. Set max_slot_wal_keep_size.

interview.q: Module 33 · Explain Monitoring Replication in a production query.
interview.answer: Monitoring tracks replication state, lag, slot retention and failover readiness. Key rules: Track pg_stat_replication. Track slot size. Alert on lag.

interview.q: Module 33 · Explain Failover Testing in a production query.
interview.answer: A failover drill measures promotion time, application reconnection and data loss against RTO and RPO. Key rules: Schedule drills. Measure RTO. Verify data.

interview.q: Module 33 · Explain Read-Your-Writes in a production query.
interview.answer: After a write, a replica may not yet show it; route that user’s next read to the primary or wait for the LSN. Key rules: Track write LSN. Route sensitive reads. Do not assume zero lag.

interview.q: Module 33 · Explain Connection Routing in a production query.
interview.answer: A router or load balancer sends writes to the primary and reads to replicas, with health checks and failover awareness. Key rules: Separate endpoints. Health-check nodes. Update routes on promotion.

interview.q: Module 33 · Explain Common Replication Errors in a production query.
interview.answer: Common failures are an inactive slot filling disk, a replica promoted while the old primary still writes, and reads routed to a lagging replica. Key rules: Monitor slots. Fence promotions. Measure lag.

interview.q: Module 33 · Explain High Availability Design in a production query.
interview.answer: High availability combines replicas, automated health checks, quorum and tested failover, not just a standby. Key rules: Redundant nodes. Health checks. Automated promotion. Client redirect.

interview.q: Module 33 · Explain Backup vs Replica in a production query.
interview.answer: A replica protects availability but does not protect against accidental deletes, corruption or ransomware without separate backups. Key rules: Replicas replicate mistakes. Keep independent backups. Test restores.

interview.q: Module 33 · Explain Practical HA Runbook in a production query.
interview.answer: A runbook makes failover deterministic: detect the failure, fence the old primary, promote the standby, redirect clients and verify writes. Key rules: Detect. Fence. Promote. Redirect. Verify.

debug.title: Writes on replica
debug.fix: INSERT INTO students (name) VALUES ('Zara') on the primary.
debug.error: cannot execute INSERT in a read-only transaction

debug.title: Replica lag read
debug.broken: Write on primary, immediately read the same row from a replica.
debug.fix: Read from the primary until the replica reaches the write LSN.
debug.error: The replica may not have the row yet

debug.title: Inactive slot
debug.fix: Drop the unused slot or restore its consumer, then monitor retained WAL.
debug.error: WAL accumulates until the disk fills

debug.title: Split brain
debug.broken: Promote the standby while the old primary is still reachable.
debug.fix: Fence the old primary first, then promote.

debug.title: Async data loss
debug.fix: Use synchronous replication for data that cannot be lost.
debug.error: A crash can lose recent commits

debug.title: Replica as backup
debug.broken: Delete the primary table and rely on the replica.
debug.error: The delete replicates to the standby

debug.title: Slot disk growth
debug.fix: Set a bound and alert on retained WAL.
debug.error: A stalled consumer can fill the disk

debug.title: Promotion without redirect
debug.fix: Promote, then update the application endpoint and verify writes.
debug.error: Clients still connect to the old primary

debug.title: Logical conflict
debug.broken: Subscription stops on a duplicate primary key.
debug.fix: Resolve the conflicting row and restart the subscription with a documented policy.
debug.error: duplicate key value violates unique constraint
